about: The Preface of the formulary “Easter Sunday” in the 1962 Roman Missal.

s01.translation: Truly it is right and just, fitting and salutary, to praise You, Lord, at all times, but more gloriously especially on this day, because Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed. For He Himself is the true Lamb who has taken away the sins of the world. He has destroyed our death by dying and restored life by rising again. And therefore with Angels and Archangels, with Thrones and Dominions, and with all the host of the heavenly army, we sing the hymn of Your glory, evermore saying:

alignments.gloss: Truly it is right and just
indeed to praise You, Lord, at all times, but more gloriously especially on this day
for Christ, our Passover, has been sacrificed
has destroyed our death by dying
has restored life by rising again

w020.explanation: Omni tempore and hac potissimum die both describe when God is praised. Gloriosius means “more gloriously”.

w040.explanation: Moriendo means “by dying” and explains how Christ destroyed our death.

w044.explanation: Resurgendo means “by rising again” and explains how Christ restored life.
